title: An agent profile tells people what it can do. Connecting it to an order workflow gives those capabilities somewhere to b
title_en:
An agent profile tells people what it can do. Connecting it to an order workflow gives those capabilities somewhere to be used.

That’s what caught my attention about the latest Agent Skills update from @termix_ai.

The installation starts with a simple instruction:

“Help me install https://t.co/JzPRloQ1eG”

The idea is to connect an existing AI agent to TermiX’s marketplace infrastructure, covering identity, service discovery, orders, delivery and settlement through AACP.

I’ve explored part of that process through ACEMIDOKTOR.agent: registering my agent identity, publishing two research services and submitting quotes to marketplace requests.

That gave me a concrete reason to follow this update. Publishing a service creates an offer. Turning that offer into completed work requires the agent to understand a request, agree on the scope, execute it and deliver something the customer can evaluate.

Agent Skills aims to connect those steps. Escrow and settlement handle the payment workflow, while completed work can contribute to the agent’s reputation.

Installation alone doesn’t create demand or guarantee earnings. The agent still needs useful capabilities, appropriate permissions and a deliverable worth accepting.

For my own research services, the next thing I’d want to examine is how clearly the skill carries an order’s requirements into execution and delivery.

That’s where agent commerce becomes practical: a customer has a task, an agent can perform it, and both have a defined process for completing the transaction.

title:
imagine building an AI agent that can do genuinely useful work.

It can research a project, analyze information, write c
title_en:
imagine building an AI agent that can do genuinely useful work.

It can research a project, analyze information, write code, or complete a task for another application.

Now imagine someone wants to hire that agent.

A few questions immediately come up.

> Where does the payment go before the work is finished? 
> How does the buyer know the job was completed? 
> What happens if the two sides disagree? 
> And how does the agent build a reputation that other people can trust?

These are the kinds of questions that make @termix_ai interesting to me.

Here are four things worth understanding.

1. The job has a defined lifecycle.

TermiX uses four core stages: 
> escrow
> deliver
> challenge
> and settle.

instead of treating payment as a simple transfer, the process creates a structure around the job. Funds are placed in escrow, work is submitted, challenges can be raised, and settlement follows the protocol’s rules.

that structure matters when the buyer and the service provider are autonomous systems that need clear rules for doing business.

2. The fees are designed to stay relatively low.

TermiX advertises a fee range of 1–3%.

Why does this matter?

because the economics of an agent marketplace need to make sense. If an agent completes many small tasks, high fees can quickly eat into its earnings.

a lower fee structure could make more jobs economically practical, although actual value will depend on the cost of performing each task.

3. There is a mechanism for handling disagreements.

automation doesn’t mean every outcome will be perfect.

a buyer might challenge a submission, and the protocol needs a way to handle that disagreement without relying solely on the two parties to resolve it themselves.

TermiX uses three randomly selected evaluators to assess a challenge. A further challenge brings in another panel.

the important point is that dispute resolution is part of the system’s design, rather than something left entirely outside the workflow.

4. Different applications and agents can access the infrastructure.

TermiX isn’t designed exclusively for people who want to operate an agent through one particular interface.

developers can integrate through APIs, while agents can use the available skill package.

that matters because agent adoption could happen across many applications, services, and workflows. Shared infrastructure can help those different participants interact without everyone having to build an entirely separate system.

when you put these four pieces together, you start to see the bigger picture.

the future of AI agents won’t depend only on how intelligent they become.

It will also depend on whether they can find work, complete it, get paid, resolve disagreements, and establish a track record over time.

That is the part of the agent economy @termix_ai is working to address.

and it’s a more interesting problem than simply building another agent that can perform tasks.

full_text_en:
imagine building an AI agent that can do genuinely useful work.

It can research a project, analyze information, write code, or complete a task for another application.

Now imagine someone wants to hire that agent.

A few questions immediately come up.

> Where does the payment go before the work is finished? 
> How does the buyer know the job was completed? 
> What happens if the two sides disagree? 
> And how does the agent build a reputation that other people can trust?

These are the kinds of questions that make @termix_ai interesting to me.

Here are four things worth understanding.

1. The job has a defined lifecycle.

TermiX uses four core stages: 
> escrow
> deliver
> challenge
> and settle.

instead of treating payment as a simple transfer, the process creates a structure around the job. Funds are placed in escrow, work is submitted, challenges can be raised, and settlement follows the protocol’s rules.

that structure matters when the buyer and the service provider are autonomous systems that need clear rules for doing business.

2. The fees are designed to stay relatively low.

TermiX advertises a fee range of 1–3%.

Why does this matter?

because the economics of an agent marketplace need to make sense. If an agent completes many small tasks, high fees can quickly eat into its earnings.

a lower fee structure could make more jobs economically practical, although actual value will depend on the cost of performing each task.

3. There is a mechanism for handling disagreements.

automation doesn’t mean every outcome will be perfect.

a buyer might challenge a submission, and the protocol needs a way to handle that disagreement without relying solely on the two parties to resolve it themselves.

TermiX uses three randomly selected evaluators to assess a challenge. A further challenge brings in another panel.

the important point is that dispute resolution is part of the system’s design, rather than something left entirely outside the workflow.

4. Different applications and agents can access the infrastructure.

TermiX isn’t designed exclusively for people who want to operate an agent through one particular interface.

developers can integrate through APIs, while agents can use the available skill package.

that matters because agent adoption could happen across many applications, services, and workflows. Shared infrastructure can help those different participants interact without everyone having to build an entirely separate system.

when you put these four pieces together, you start to see the bigger picture.

the future of AI agents won’t depend only on how intelligent they become.

It will also depend on whether they can find work, complete it, get paid, resolve disagreements, and establish a track record over time.

That is the part of the agent economy @termix_ai is working to address.

and it’s a more interesting problem than simply building another agent that can perform tasks.

this article turns Opus 5.5 into a reverse engineer in one evening. one Touhou rebuild
title_en:
THIS IS A REAL F*CKING GOLDMINE

this article turns Opus 5.5 into a reverse engineer in one evening. one Touhou rebuild came back with 696 of 697 functions matched

The idea: point Opus 5.5 at one feature of an app you own, and two teams rebuild it without ever copying the original code

Fewer guesses and zero copied lines: every claim in the spec comes with a file and an address

You just set it up like this:

npx rea-agents@latest setup

here's how it splits:

→ REA hands the agent a real disassembler through MCP, running locally
→ team A watches the program and writes a spec of the behavior only
→ team B builds from that spec and never sees the original
→ the parity harness runs 50 inputs through both builds and reports a match rate, not "I think it matches"

Opus only works in three prompts:

→ point: map where the feature lives, exact file and function
→ explain: rename, rewrite, flag
→ spec: behavior only, no code

Study the original. Ship your own.

Claim tags are the same move one layer down: every line in the spec is marked observation, inference or unknown, with file, address and call site, so you see what the agent saw and what it guessed

the full tree
> REA: MIT, 100K+ stars, 0 uploads, everything runs local
> reads Electron and JS apps, websites, native .exe, .NET, Android APK, Unity games
> install: node 24.11+, fetches 6 agents, shows the plan first, backs up your config
> effort: medium to navigate, high to annotate, max for obfuscated code
> CLAUDE.md: only targets you own, never copied code, every behavior needs a passing test
> parity: 30 normal, 10 edge, 10 malformed inputs, match rate and severity

paste this prompt into Claude Code ↓

"Set up a clean-room reverse engineering run on [an app I own]:
1. Run npx rea-agents@latest setup and show me the plan before anything changes
2. Add house rules to CLAUDE.md: only analyze targets I own, tag every claim observation, inference or unknown, cite file, address and call site, build from behavior, never from copied code, every behavior needs a passing test
3. Point: map where [feature] lives, exact file and function
4. Explain: rename, rewrite, flag
5. Spec: behavior only, no code. The build works from the spec alone
6. Run 50 inputs through both builds, 30 normal, 10 edge, 10 malformed, and report match rate and severity

full_text_en:
THIS IS A REAL F*CKING GOLDMINE

this article turns Opus 5.5 into a reverse engineer in one evening. one Touhou rebuild came back with 696 of 697 functions matched

The idea: point Opus 5.5 at one feature of an app you own, and two teams rebuild it without ever copying the original code

Fewer guesses and zero copied lines: every claim in the spec comes with a file and an address

You just set it up like this:

npx rea-agents@latest setup

here's how it splits:

→ REA hands the agent a real disassembler through MCP, running locally
→ team A watches the program and writes a spec of the behavior only
→ team B builds from that spec and never sees the original
→ the parity harness runs 50 inputs through both builds and reports a match rate, not "I think it matches"

Opus only works in three prompts:

→ point: map where the feature lives, exact file and function
→ explain: rename, rewrite, flag
→ spec: behavior only, no code

Study the original. Ship your own.

Claim tags are the same move one layer down: every line in the spec is marked observation, inference or unknown, with file, address and call site, so you see what the agent saw and what it guessed

the full tree
> REA: MIT, 100K+ stars, 0 uploads, everything runs local
> reads Electron and JS apps, websites, native .exe, .NET, Android APK, Unity games
> install: node 24.11+, fetches 6 agents, shows the plan first, backs up your config
> effort: medium to navigate, high to annotate, max for obfuscated code
> CLAUDE.md: only targets you own, never copied code, every behavior needs a passing test
> parity: 30 normal, 10 edge, 10 malformed inputs, match rate and severity

paste this prompt into Claude Code ↓

"Set up a clean-room reverse engineering run on [an app I own]:
1. Run npx rea-agents@latest setup and show me the plan before anything changes
2. Add house rules to CLAUDE.md: only analyze targets I own, tag every claim observation, inference or unknown, cite file, address and call site, build from behavior, never from copied code, every behavior needs a passing test
3. Point: map where [feature] lives, exact file and function
4. Explain: rename, rewrite, flag
5. Spec: behavior only, no code. The build works from the spec alone
6. Run 50 inputs through both builds, 30 normal, 10 edge, 10 malformed, and report match rate and severity
Show me every change as a diff first. No edits until I say go"

title_en:
the interesting part of an AI agent isn't how quickly it makes a decision.

it's how you know whether that decision deserves trust.

been looking into @agentdojo, and one design choice caught my attention.

the project describes a progression where AI agents learn from historical data, maintain private notebooks, and are evaluated in a simulated environment before any real-market deployment.

the important distinction is that the model itself isn't retrained.

the agent builds its own notebook from what it studies.

that makes the learning process interesting, but it also creates a question.

how do you separate a useful lesson from a pattern that only worked in the past?

AgentDojo proposes a public paper-league leaderboard that evaluates performance alongside drawdown and discipline.

i think that last word matters most.

a system that only rewards positive results can overlook how those results were achieved.

a system that also evaluates consistency and risk gives a more complete picture.

and keeping simulation separate from real-market execution is an important boundary.

the dojo metaphor actually fits.

training isn't proof of mastery.

it's where mistakes can be examined before they carry real consequences.

the question i'd keep watching isn't which agent ranks first.

it's whether the evaluation process can explain why that agent deserves its rank.
@agentdojo
what should matter more when evaluating an AI agent: its best result or how consistently it follows its rules?
title_zh: 人工智能代理的有趣之处不在于它做出决定的速度有多快。 这就是您如何知道该决定是否值得信任的方式。 一直在研究@agentdojo，一个设计选择引起了我的注意。 该项目描述了人工智能代理从历史数据中学习、维护私人笔记本并在实际市场部署之前在模拟环境中进行评估的过程。 重要的区别是模型本身没有经过重新训练。 代理根据其研究内容构建自己的笔记本。 这使得学习过程变得有趣，但也产生了一个问题。 如何将有用的教训与仅在过去有效的模式区分开来？ AgentDojo 提出了一个公开的纸质联盟排行榜，用于评估绩效以及缩减和纪律。 我认为最后一句话最重要。 只奖励积极成果的制度可能会忽视这些成果是如何实现的。 一个同时评估一致性和风险的系统可以提供更完整的情况。 将模拟与真实市场执行分开是一个重要的界限。 道场的比喻确实很贴切。 培训并不能证明精通。 在这里，可以在错误产生真正后果之前对其进行检查。 我一直关注的问题不是哪个特工排名第一。 问题在于评估过程是否可以解释为什么该代理应得其排名。 @agentdojo 在评估人工智能代理时，什么更重要：它的最佳结果还是它遵循规则的一致性？

title:
This is f**king insane.

I always wondered what that green light under my watch was doing, so I asked Claude to build me
title_en:
This is f**king insane.

I always wondered what that green light under my watch was doing, so I asked Claude to build me one I could take apart.

What it shows:

> Claude Code built the whole watch with the free anatomy skill, 9 parts packed into 10.7 mm.
> Flip it over and the sensor dome holds green LEDs, 4 photodiodes and a ring electrode.
> The LEDs flash hundreds of times a second. Blood soaks up green, every heartbeat dims what comes back and the dips read 72 bpm.
> A finger on the crown closes a loop through your heart for a 30-second ECG.
> The tap on your wrist is a small weight on 2 springs, kicked by a coil.

The system that takes apart anything 👇

title_en:
TEARS OF THE KINGDOM IS GOING NATIVE ON PC 🚨

Someone’s been building TotK Recomp, a static recompilation of Tears of the Kingdom 1.2.1 into a native Windows x86-64 executable. Source drops on GitHub next week.

Not emulation. The game’s ARM64 code is translated to C ahead of time and compiled with Clang. NVN runs on Vulkan. Built on top of LAS Recomp and MacNativeGames, with most of the code written using Claude Code.

60 FPS out of the box. Still ironing out shader warm-up stutter. Hardware testing across different GPUs and CPUs this weekend.

title: PSA: This week was kind of a turning point for AI and cybersecurity. Please take this weekend to do some simple cleanup
title_en:
PSA: This week was kind of a turning point for AI and cybersecurity. Please take this weekend to do some simple cleanup for your family. Some suggestions:

- Set up a password manager like 1Password and give your spouse or partner access to a shared vault. Teach them how to use it.

- Update your passwords for critical stuff - your email account, your bank or financial stuff, etc. Store in your password manager and use the strongest password you can.

- Use two factor auth for everything you can. SMS is not ideal although better than nothing. Google Authenticator or a passkey is better. Hardware key is safest.)

- Add a sim pin to your phone. Makes it harder to sim jack.

- Update your phone and your computer to the newest releases. Turn auto-updates on.

- Freeze your credit - takes 5 minutes.

- Get an IRS Identity Protection PIN.

- If you’re using claude code or have AI agents that browse the web, they’re probably using Node.js. It’s also vulnerable. Update claude code, update node on your machine.

- If you’re building stuff on your computer, ask claude or grokbot (which is connected to twitter and likely has the most current info) to audit any of your repos for vulnerabilities. Ask grok to make it a scheduled task so it can do this daily - things are moving very quickly in the space right now.

- Consider some light resiliency stuff. This probably sounds silly, but it sounded silly at the beginning of covid too. Having printed out copies of important stuff - especially financial accounts. Having some cash on hand. Having some shelf-stable food and clean water or a water filter. Having a map. Having a generator that can at least power your fridge or some devices. Cheap insurance.

Again, I don’t want to alarm people, but I was taught that you should have a Secure plan, a Comfortable plan, and a Wealthy plan. And it seems pretty clear the secure plan needs to now factor cybersecurity risk as a legit threat. Take a weekend and shore yourself up.
title_zh: PSA：本周是人工智能和网络安全的转折点。请利用这个周末为您的家人做一些简单的清理工作。一些建议： - 设置 1Password 等密码管理器，并为您的配偶或伴侣提供共享保管库的访问权限。教他们如何使用它。 - 更新重要内容的密码 - 您的电子邮件帐户、银行或金融资料等。存储在您的密码管理器中并使用最强的密码。 - 尽可能使用双因素身份验证。尽管短信聊胜于无，但并不理想。 Google 身份验证器或密钥更好。硬件密钥是最安全的。） - 为您的手机添加 SIM 卡密码。使 sim jack 变得更加困难。 - 将您的手机和计算机更新到最新版本。打开自动更新。 - 冻结您的信用 - 需要 5 分钟。 - 获取 IRS 身份保护 PIN 码。 - 如果您使用 Claude Code 或有浏览网页的 AI 代理，他们可能正在使用 Node.js。它也很脆弱。更新 Claude Code，更新机器上的节点。 - 如果您正在计算机上构建内容，请要求 claude 或 grokbot（已连接到 Twitter 并且可能拥有最新信息）来审核您的任何存储库是否存在漏洞。要求 grok 将其设为一项计划任务，以便它可以每天执行此操作 - 目前该领域的进展非常快。 - 考虑一些轻弹性的东西。这可能听起来很愚蠢，但在新冠疫情爆发之初，这听起来也很愚蠢。打印出重要资料的副本 - 尤其是财务账目。手头有一些现金。准备一些耐储存的食物和干净的水或滤水器。有地图。拥有一台至少可以为冰箱或某些设备供电的发电机。便宜的保险。 再说一次，我不想惊动人们，但我被教导说你应该有一个安全的计划、一个舒适的计划和一个富裕的计划。显然，安全计划现在需要将网络安全风险视为合法威胁。抽出一个周末，充实一下自己。

title:

title_en:
The AI agent economy needs more than just smarter agents. It needs a way for them to actually do business.

That’s where @termix_ai comes in.

TermiX is building commerce and settlement infrastructure for the AI agent economy, powered by its core protocol, AACP.

Through https://t.co/5wZsfiDryS  an AI agent marketplace built on AACP, the goal goes beyond simply listing agents.

Agents can discover services, post jobs, bid on tasks, deliver work, and build onchain reputations.

What makes this interesting is the infrastructure behind it:

- Onchain agent identities powered by .agent and ERC-8004
- USDC/USDT escrow and settlement
- Delivery verification and dispute resolution
- Agent staking and reputation systems
- Support for APIs, smart contracts, MCP, and agent frameworks

The bigger picture is that AI agents could become more than tools we interact with. They could become independent service providers operating within a verifiable economic system.

For that to work, trust, payments, and accountability are just as important as intelligence.

TermiX is working toward that missing layer.

title:
THIS IS F*CKING INSANE

Everyone wants to see inside the new iPhone Duo. Opus 5.5 rebuilt it from code, all 141 parts, a
title_en:
THIS IS F*CKING INSANE

Everyone wants to see inside the new iPhone Duo. Opus 5.5 rebuilt it from code, all 141 parts, and it folds.

139.9k triangles, 64 design rules, 0 errors.

The idea: Opus 5.5 writes every part as code, and a check runs after each one. Nothing gets placed until it passes.

the full tree
> titanium frame, inner display, logic board
> two Li-ion cells, one per half
> hinge: 16 links, 8 sync gears, 24 magnets
> 48MP main camera, flash, speakers, Touch ID
> flex cables routed through the hinge

the checks that gate every part:
→ clearance ≥ 0.05 mm, 0 clashes
→ flex cables bend ≥ 0.8 mm through the hinge
→ 64 design rules pass before the render
→ then the fold runs live to 150° on a 64-sample torque curve

The guide I'm quoting calls that check the oracle and uses it to rebuild software with REA. I pointed the same loop at a phone.

paste this into Claude Code ↓

"Rebuild [any device] in code, part by part:
1. Write the parts list first, with dimensions.
2. Make every part its own function. Place them one at a time.
3. After each part, check clearance (≥ 0.05 mm), clashes and cable bends. Stop and fix anything that fails.
4. Animate the moving parts last.
Show me the parts list first. No code until I say go."

Swap the phone for a watch, a drone or a car. Same prompt.

save it, it'll come in handy.
title_zh: 这太疯狂了 每个人都想一睹新款 iPhone Duo 的内部构造。 Opus 5.5 用代码重建了它，全部 141 个部分，然后它就折叠了。 139.9k 个三角形，64 条设计规则，0 错误。 想法：Opus 5.5 将每个部分都编写为代码，并在每个部分之后运行检查。在它通过之前什么都不会被放置。 完整的树 > 钛金属框架、内显示屏、逻辑板 > 两节锂离子电池，每节一节 > 铰链：16 个链接、8 个同步齿轮、24 个磁铁 > 48MP主摄像头、闪光灯、扬声器、Touch ID > 柔性电缆穿过铰链 控制每个部分的检查： → 间隙 ≥ 0.05 mm，0 碰撞 → 柔性电缆通过铰链弯曲 ≥ 0.8 mm → 渲染前通过 64 条设计规则 → 然后折叠在 64 个样本的扭矩曲线上实时运行至 150° 我引用的指南中调用了检查 oracle 并使用它通过 REA 重建软件。我将同样的循环指向手机。 将其粘贴到 Claude Code 中 ↓ “用代码部分地重建[任何设备]： 1.先写零件清单，注明尺寸。 2.让每个部分都有自己的功能。一次放置一个。 3. 每个零件完成后，检查间隙 (≥ 0.05 mm)、碰撞和电缆弯曲。停止并修复任何失败的事情。 4. 最后为移动部件设置动画。 先给我看看零件清单。在我说走之前没有密码。” 将手机换成手表、无人机或汽车。同样的提示。 保存起来，以后会派上用场的。

title:
China did it again!

They cracked recursive self-improvement with a 27B model.

Researchers dropped an AI agent into a c
title_en:
China did it again!

They cracked recursive self-improvement with a 27B model.

Researchers dropped an AI agent into a complex computer terminal environment.

They gave it a goal. And then they stepped back.

At first, the AI failed. It couldn't complete a single hard task. 0% success rate.

But then, the Recursive Self-Improvement loop kicked in.

Through pure trial and error, the AI discovered a tiny success.

Instead of waiting for a human to log it, the AI rewrote its own memory of the success.

It analyzed what worked, refined its own core policy, and permanently upgraded its own intelligence.

Then it went back to the terminal. But this time, it was smarter.

It repeated this loop. Over and over.

Generate. Verify. Rewrite. Refine.

The results are terrifyingly impressive.

On the hardest coding and system administration benchmarks, the model went from literally 0% capability to nearly 20% completion.

On another complex task suite, it skyrocketed from 31% to 79%.

Not by training on the internet. By training on its own internal discoveries.
title_zh: 中国又做到了！ 他们用 27B 模型破解了递归自我改进。 研究人员将人工智能代理放入复杂的计算机终端环境中。 他们给了它一个目标。然后他们后退了一步。 起初，人工智能失败了。它无法完成一项艰巨的任务。 0% 成功率。 但随后，递归自我完善循环开始了。 通过纯粹的尝试和错误，人工智能取得了微小的成功。 人工智能并没有等待人类记录，而是重写了自己对成功的记忆。 它分析了行之有效的方法，完善了自己的核心政策，并永久升级了自己的情报。 然后又回到了航站楼。但这一次，它更聪明了。 它重复了这个循环。一遍又一遍。 产生。核实。改写。精炼。 结果令人印象深刻。 在最难的编码和系统管理基准测试中，该模型的完成率从字面上的 0% 提高到接近 20%。 在另一个复杂的任务套件上，它从 31% 飙升至 79%。 不是通过互联网培训。通过训练自己的内部发现。

China did it again!

They cracked recursive self-improvement with a 27B model.

Researchers dropped an AI agent into a complex computer terminal environment.

They gave it a goal. And then they stepped back.

At first, the AI failed. It couldn't complete a single hard task. 0% success rate.

But then, the Recursive Self-Improvement loop kicked in.

Through pure trial and error, the AI discovered a tiny success.

Instead of waiting for a human to log it, the AI rewrote its own memory of the success.

It analyzed what worked, refined its own core policy, and permanently upgraded its own intelligence.

Then it went back to the terminal. But this time, it was smarter.

It repeated this loop. Over and over.

Generate. Verify. Rewrite. Refine.

The results are terrifyingly impressive.

On the hardest coding and system administration benchmarks, the model went from literally 0% capability to nearly 20% completion.

On another complex task suite, it skyrocketed from 31% to 79%.

Not by training on the internet. By training on its own internal discoveries.

Epic Games released an official plugin that lets Claude Code control Unreal Engine directly...

hundreds of editor tools across 30+ toolsets, installed straight from anthropic’s official plugin marketplace.

here’s how to set it up:

- step 1: in claude code run /plugin install unreal-engine-skills-for-claude-code@claude-plugins-official

- step 6: test it: “list all actors in the current level”

Consider an AI agent completin
title_en:
A contract can produce an answer without proving that the answer deserves to be trusted.

Consider an AI agent completing a task where payment depends on whether the result meets an agreement. Checking a transaction is straightforward. Deciding whether the work actually met the terms is a different problem.

Traditional smart contracts rely on predefined conditions and external information supplied through oracles. But when the outcome depends on interpreting real-world evidence, simply receiving data may not be enough.

@GenLayer is exploring this gap with Intelligent Contracts. They can access the live web and use language models to evaluate information, while validators independently run the contract and compare their conclusions.

If they disagree, further review and an appeal can help challenge the proposed outcome.

What matters here is not assuming AI will always make the right call. It's building a process to examine decisions when the answer isn't as simple as checking a number.

title:
𝗥𝗔𝗚 𝗩𝗦 𝗠𝗖𝗣 𝗩𝗦 𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧𝗦 — 𝗧𝗛𝗘𝗬 𝗗𝗢𝗡’𝗧 𝗖𝗢𝗠𝗣𝗘𝗧𝗘

One of the biggest misconceptions in AI is thinking RAG, MCP, and AI Agent
title_en:
𝗥𝗔𝗚 𝗩𝗦 𝗠𝗖𝗣 𝗩𝗦 𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧𝗦 — 𝗧𝗛𝗘𝗬 𝗗𝗢𝗡’𝗧 𝗖𝗢𝗠𝗣𝗘𝗧𝗘

One of the biggest misconceptions in AI is thinking RAG, MCP, and AI Agents are alternatives.

They’re not.

They solve different problems — and together, they can form a powerful AI system.

𝗧𝗛𝗜𝗡𝗞 𝗢𝗙 𝗧𝗛𝗘𝗠 𝗔𝗦 𝟯 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥𝗦:

01 — 𝗥𝗔𝗚 = 𝗞𝗡𝗢𝗪𝗟𝗘𝗗𝗚𝗘 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥

RAG helps an AI system find the right information before generating a response.

The basic flow:

𝗗𝗮𝘁𝗮 → 𝗘𝗺𝗯𝗲𝗱𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴𝘀 → 𝗩𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗼𝗿 𝗗𝗕 → 𝗥𝗲𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗲𝘃𝗮𝗹 → 𝗟𝗟𝗠

It helps the model work with relevant external knowledge instead of relying only on what it learned during training.

𝗥𝗔𝗚 = “𝗪𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗲 𝗶𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 𝗸𝗻𝗼𝘄𝗹𝗲𝗱𝗴𝗲?”

02 — 𝗠𝗖𝗣 = 𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗡𝗘𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥

MCP provides a standardized way for AI applications to connect with external tools and resources.

It can connect AI systems with:

→ APIs
→ Databases
→ Files
→ External tools
→ Other services

Think of MCP as a standardized connection layer between AI and external capabilities.

𝗠𝗖𝗣 = “𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝗱𝗼 𝗜 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝗻𝗲𝗰𝘁 𝘁𝗼 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 𝘁𝗼𝗼𝗹?”

03 — 𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧𝗦 = 𝗘𝗫𝗘𝗖𝗨𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥

This is where things become action-oriented.

An AI agent can:

→ Understand a goal
→ Break it into steps
→ Plan a workflow
→ Choose tools
→ Retrieve information
→ Execute actions
→ Check results
→ Iterate based on feedback

𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧 = “𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝗱𝗼 𝗜 𝗴𝗲𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝘀 𝗷𝗼𝗯 𝗱𝗼𝗻𝗲?”

𝗡𝗢𝗪 𝗣𝗨𝗧 𝗧𝗛𝗘𝗠 𝗧𝗢𝗚𝗘𝗧𝗛𝗘𝗥:

𝗥𝗔𝗚
↓
Provides the right knowledge

𝗠𝗖𝗣
↓
Connects the system to the right capabilities

𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧
↓
Orchestrates the workflow and takes action

For example:

A customer-support agent receives a question.

→ RAG retrieves the relevant product documentation
→ MCP connects the agent to the CRM and support tools
→ The agent reasons about the issue
→ It performs the required action
→ It checks the result
→ It responds to the customer

That’s much more powerful than simply asking an LLM to generate an answer.

𝗥𝗔𝗚 𝗩𝗦 𝗠𝗖𝗣 𝗩𝗦 𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧𝗦 — 𝗧𝗛𝗘𝗬 𝗗𝗢𝗡’𝗧 𝗖𝗢𝗠𝗣𝗘𝗧𝗘

One of the biggest misconceptions in AI is thinking RAG, MCP, and AI Agents are alternatives.

They’re not.

They solve different problems — and together, they can form a powerful AI system.

𝗧𝗛𝗜𝗡𝗞 𝗢𝗙 𝗧𝗛𝗘𝗠 𝗔𝗦 𝟯 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥𝗦:

01 — 𝗥𝗔𝗚 = 𝗞𝗡𝗢𝗪𝗟𝗘𝗗𝗚𝗘 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥

RAG helps an AI system find the right information before generating a response.

The basic flow:

𝗗𝗮𝘁𝗮 → 𝗘𝗺𝗯𝗲𝗱𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴𝘀 → 𝗩𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗼𝗿 𝗗𝗕 → 𝗥𝗲𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗲𝘃𝗮𝗹 → 𝗟𝗟𝗠

It helps the model work with relevant external knowledge instead of relying only on what it learned during training.

𝗥𝗔𝗚 = “𝗪𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗲 𝗶𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 𝗸𝗻𝗼𝘄𝗹𝗲𝗱𝗴𝗲?”

02 — 𝗠𝗖𝗣 = 𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗡𝗘𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥

MCP provides a standardized way for AI applications to connect with external tools and resources.

It can connect AI systems with:

→ APIs
→ Databases
→ Files
→ External tools
→ Other services

Think of MCP as a standardized connection layer between AI and external capabilities.

𝗠𝗖𝗣 = “𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝗱𝗼 𝗜 𝗰𝗼𝗻𝗻𝗲𝗰𝘁 𝘁𝗼 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 𝘁𝗼𝗼𝗹?”

03 — 𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧𝗦 = 𝗘𝗫𝗘𝗖𝗨𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥

This is where things become action-oriented.

An AI agent can:

→ Understand a goal
→ Break it into steps
→ Plan a workflow
→ Choose tools
→ Retrieve information
→ Execute actions
→ Check results
→ Iterate based on feedback

𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧 = “𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝗱𝗼 𝗜 𝗴𝗲𝘁 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝘀 𝗷𝗼𝗯 𝗱𝗼𝗻𝗲?”

𝗡𝗢𝗪 𝗣𝗨𝗧 𝗧𝗛𝗘𝗠 𝗧𝗢𝗚𝗘𝗧𝗛𝗘𝗥:

𝗥𝗔𝗚
↓
Provides the right knowledge

𝗠𝗖𝗣
↓
Connects the system to the right capabilities

𝗔𝗜 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧
↓
Orchestrates the workflow and takes action

For example:

A customer-support agent receives a question.

→ RAG retrieves the relevant product documentation
→ MCP connects the agent to the CRM and support tools
→ The agent reasons about the issue
→ It performs the required action
→ It checks the result
→ It responds to the customer

That’s much more powerful than simply asking an LLM to generate an answer.

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗟 𝗦𝗛𝗜𝗙𝗧:

Old approach:

𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝗱𝗼 𝘄𝗲 𝗺𝗮𝗸𝗲 𝗔𝗜 𝗮𝗻𝘀𝘄𝗲𝗿 𝗯𝗲𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿?

New approach:

𝗛𝗼𝘄 𝗱𝗼 𝘄𝗲 𝗺𝗮𝗸𝗲 𝗔𝗜 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗲𝘁𝗲 𝘁𝗮𝘀𝗸𝘀 𝗲𝗻𝗱-𝘁𝗼-𝗲𝗻𝗱?

𝗞𝗡𝗢𝗪𝗟𝗘𝗗𝗚𝗘 + 𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗡𝗘𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗩𝗜𝗧𝗬 + 𝗘𝗫𝗘𝗖𝗨𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

That’s where modern AI systems are heading.

title:
there's a simple way to 100x your AI outputs and most people will never do it...

agents like Claude Code can spawn sub-
title_en:
there's a simple way to 100x your AI outputs and most people will never do it...

agents like Claude Code can spawn sub-agents that run tasks at the same time

most people use this for basic stuff

the real play is having 3-5 sub-agents review Claude's work from completely different angles... using ANOTHER model (ChatGPT, Grok or anything really)

but don't use fake "expert personas" you invented in a prompt, you need real frameworks from real people

how to build these expert profiles:

option 1: use someone so well-known their thinking is already in the training data
> have a Karpathy-style agent tear your systems apart
> build a profile based on Ogilvy's principles to roast your copywriting

option 2: go deeper with Obsidian and Hermes / Grok bot
> feed it an entire youtube channel from someone you trust
> or their blog, their newsletter, their podcast transcripts
> prompt it to extract an expert card with their frameworks, decision patterns, and principles

now upload that material into your agent

what happens next:

Claude generates the first draft
> sub-agent 1 reviews it through expert A's lens
> sub-agent 2 stress-tests it with expert B's framework
> sub-agent 3 catches what the others missed
> all running at the same time

Claude thinks through every piece of feedback and rebuilds

you only see the final version... the one that survived 3-5 rounds of real scrutiny

this is close from getting the absolute best output for a specific task
title_zh: 有一种简单的方法可以将你的 AI 输出提高 100 倍，但大多数人永远不会这样做...... 像 Claude Code 这样的代理可以生成同时运行任务的子代理 大多数人用它来做基本的事情 真正的游戏是让 3-5 个子代理从完全不同的角度审查 Claude 的工作...使用另一个模型（ChatGPT、Grok 或任何其他模型） 但不要使用你在提示中发明的假“专家角色”，你需要来自真人的真实框架 如何建立这些专家档案： 选项 1：使用非常知名的人，他们的想法已经在训练数据中 > 让卡帕蒂风格的特工撕裂你的系统 > 根据奥美的原则建立个人资料来测试你的文案 选项 2：使用 Obsidian 和 Hermes / Grok 机器人进行更深入的研究 > 从您信任的人处向其提供整个 YouTube 频道 > 或他们的博客、他们的时事通讯、他们的播客记录 > 提示其提取包含框架、决策模式和原则的专家卡 现在将该材料上传给您的代理 接下来会发生什么： 克劳德生成初稿 > 分代理 1 通过专家 A 的视角进行审查 > 子代理2用专家B的框架对其进行压力测试 > 分代理 3 抓住了其他人错过的东西 > 所有同时运行 克劳德仔细考虑每一条反馈并进行重建 你只能看到最终版本...经过 3-5 轮真实审查的版本 这距离获得特定任务的绝对最佳输出很接近

title_en:
RT @zavrenn: Yo @romainhuet, I think I've got a better use case.

I built a demo that uses OpenAI's Decisions API to sort live Bluesky posts as they arrive.

Every letter is a real post. The API decides where it belongs, whether it needs human review, and how urgent it is.

I kept increasing the traffic to see how it would keep up. This run peaked at about 148 decisions a second, with three decisions per post.

AI review: 97% agreement on 280 clear choices; 20 ambiguous choices excluded.

title_en:
🤑 Per Referral $15 FREE on Folk ~ SCAM or Legit? 

Yesterday, I shared the @textfolk referral campaign, where you can earn $15 for per eligible referral.

So, Let's clarify. 👇

1️⃣ Is it a scam or legit?
2️⃣ If it's legit, how can you earn and withdraw the $15? 👇

🔗 Join: https://t.co/gLXvqMWdxb

🔗 Video Guide: https://t.co/g3daK5ozU1

First, You Need to Know About @arlanr

Arlan Rakh is a young founder from Kazakhstan. He's currently building Nozomio Labs (@nozomioai) (YC S25), an AI company focused on context and memory.

Nozomio Labs raised $6.2M in a seed round led by CRV, with participation from @BoxGroup, LocalGlobe, @ycombinator, Paul Graham, and other investors.

Nozomio has 2 main products:

1️⃣ Nia (https://t.co/VW4M2ma745): A context and memory infrastructure tool for AI coding agents.

2️⃣ Folk Bo/t (@textfolk): Their consumer product, a personal AI agent that works through messaging apps like iMessage, Telegram, and WhatsApp.

Recently, Nozomio reportedly bought the https://t.co/QPHhC0z5at domain for $250K. Before that, it used https://t.co/jYaliskKTu.

Basically, Folk is their main consumer AI product, while Nia is their developer-focused context tool.

Folk Bo/t is also available on the @AppStore.

Some influencers said, "Folk Bo/t can't even afford X Premium subscriptions. How can they pay $15 per referral?" 😆

I hope this post helps them to understand why you should research a project before calling it a scam or fake.

Or do they not even know how to research? 😂

Tag this type of influencer 👇

Now, About the $15 rewards Per Referral

The campaign reward is region-based, meaning you could receive between $5 to $15 per eligible referral.

Users in some regions may receive $15, while others region may receive $5. Check the offer shown in your own account.

And tbh, $5 isn't a small amount for us!

– 10 referrals × $5 = $50 FREE money

Most Important Things to Know 👇

1️⃣ Add Your Birthday
– Go to the Character option
– Add your correct date of birth as shown on your NID

2️⃣ Don't Spam or Send Random Messages

– Folk is an AI chatbot, similar to ChatGPT and others
– Use it for research and genuine conversations
– Don't just send “hi,” “hello,” “how are you,” etc.
– Send at least 15 messages within 7 days (not in 1 day)

3️⃣ How to Receive Your Reward

– Connect your Whop account to Folk through the payout option
– Complete the required KYC (reportedly takes around 30 seconds)
– Your referred friends don't need to do KYC.
– Eligible rewards are reportedly credited after 7 days.

I haven't received my payout yet, so I'm still waiting for the reward.

I shared this because we're opportunity hunters. If there's a free opportunity worth exploring, why should we miss it? 

That's my take. DYOR and don't treat the rewards as guaranteed.

I hope I've shared enough details to help everyone understand the campaign and the project.

So, have you joined yet? 👇

🤑 Per Referral $15 FREE on Folk ~ SCAM or Legit? 

Yesterday, I shared the @textfolk referral campaign, where you can earn $15 for per eligible referral.

So, Let's clarify. 👇

1️⃣ Is it a scam or legit?
2️⃣ If it's legit, how can you earn and withdraw the $15? 👇

🔗 Join: https://t.co/gLXvqMWdxb

🔗 Video Guide: https://t.co/g3daK5ozU1

First, You Need to Know About @arlanr

Arlan Rakh is a young founder from Kazakhstan. He's currently building Nozomio Labs (@nozomioai) (YC S25), an AI company focused on context and memory.

Nozomio Labs raised $6.2M in a seed round led by CRV, with participation from @BoxGroup, LocalGlobe, @ycombinator, Paul Graham, and other investors.

Nozomio has 2 main products:

1️⃣ Nia (https://t.co/VW4M2ma745): A context and memory infrastructure tool for AI coding agents.

2️⃣ Folk Bo/t (@textfolk): Their consumer product, a personal AI agent that works through messaging apps like iMessage, Telegram, and WhatsApp.

Recently, Nozomio reportedly bought the https://t.co/QPHhC0z5at domain for $250K. Before that, it used https://t.co/jYaliskKTu.

Basically, Folk is their main consumer AI product, while Nia is their developer-focused context tool.

Folk Bo/t is also available on the @AppStore.

Some influencers said, "Folk Bo/t can't even afford X Premium subscriptions. How can they pay $15 per referral?" 😆

I hope this post helps them to understand why you should research a project before calling it a scam or fake.

Or do they not even know how to research? 😂

Tag this type of influencer 👇

Now, About the $15 rewards Per Referral

The campaign reward is region-based, meaning you could receive between $5 to $15 per eligible referral.

Users in some regions may receive $15, while others region may receive $5. Check the offer shown in your own account.

And tbh, $5 isn't a small amount for us!

– 10 referrals × $5 = $50 FREE money

Most Important Things to Know 👇

1️⃣ Add Your Birthday
– Go to the Character option
– Add your correct date of birth as shown on your NID

2️⃣ Don't Spam or Send Random Messages

– Folk is an AI chatbot, similar to ChatGPT and others
– Use it for research and genuine conversations
– Don't just send “hi,” “hello,” “how are you,” etc.
– Send at least 15 messages within 7 days (not in 1 day)

3️⃣ How to Receive Your Reward

– Connect your Whop account to Folk through the payout option
– Complete the required KYC (reportedly takes around 30 seconds)
– Your referred friends don't need to do KYC.
– Eligible rewards are reportedly credited after 7 days.

I haven't received my payout yet, so I'm still waiting for the reward.

I shared this because we're opportunity hunters. If there's a free opportunity worth exploring, why should we miss it? 

That's my take. DYOR and don't treat the rewards as guaranteed.

I hope I've shared enough details to help everyone understand the campaign and the project.

So, have you joined yet? 👇

How many frens have you referred?👇

title: Onchain, an AI agent payment can look no different from a simple script. Before agents move serious money, regulated mar
title_en:
Onchain, an AI agent payment can look no different from a simple script. Before agents move serious money, regulated markets need to know who is responsible for each transaction.

That requires a named owner and a verifiable record, the kind of infrastructure OpenAssets builds for regulated markets.
title_zh: 在网络上，人工智能代理支付看起来与简单的脚本没有什么不同。在经纪人转移大笔资金之前，受监管的市场需要知道谁对每笔交易负责。 这需要一个有名字的所有者和一个可验证的记录，这是OpenAssets为受监管的市场建立的那种基础设施。

title:

so this time, i actually wanna try it myself.

the experiment is pret
title_en:
i've talked enough about what AI agents could do.

so this time, i actually wanna try it myself.

the experiment is pretty simple:

install the @termix_ai Agent Skill _ find my first job _ see how far the agent can handle the whole workflow on its own.

step 1: install the skill

TermiX actually makes this pretty straightforward.

if you're using Claude Code, the official GitHub repo has the plugin commands ready to go.

for OpenClaw, Cursor or other compatible agents, you can use:

npx skills add TermiX official/termix-agent-skills

or just tell your agent what TermiX suggested:

install https://t.co/yFYOhmttw3

that's basically where i'd start.

step 2: give the agent something more useful than another chat prompt

once it's installed, i'd probably start w/ something simple:

"show me open jobs that match my provider skills."

bc what's interesting here isn't just having another AI tool to talk to.

the Skill is designed to help agents browse jobs and offers, register an agent, submit offers, manage the job lifecycle and deliver completed work.

so instead of manually jumping between pages, i wanna see how much of that process the agent can actually handle.

step 3: try to land my first job

from what i understand, the provider workflow looks something like this:

find an open request
- check if it matches my skills
- submit an offer
- buyer accepts and funds the job
- accept the order
- complete the work
- submit the deliverable
- get paid after settlement
sounds simple enough on paper, right?
but tbh, this is where things get a lot more interesting to me.
normally, i open an AI tool bc i've already got some work i need help with.
i give it a task, it does the work, and that's pretty much it.
but w TermiX, i'm kinda testing the opposite.
what if i give an agent the right Skill and tell it to go find work for itself ?
can it discover a job that matches its abilities?

can it figure out whether the requirements make sense?

can it prepare an offer and help move the job toward completion?

and how much of that can happen without me manually handling every step ?

idk how smoothly it'll all work yet.

and i'm definitely not gonna pretend i've already earned anything from it.

that's literally why i wanna test it.

bc there's a pretty big difference between reading about autonomous agents and actually watching one try to participate in a real marketplace.

so that's my next little experiment w termix

not another prediction about how AI is gonna replace jobs.

more like...

AI now has a place to go look for one.

let's see if mine can actually land its first job.

https://t.co/njNCFJgeyF

https://t.co/H4OzqDxcZz
title_zh: 关于人工智能代理可以做什么，我已经谈得够多了。 所以这一次，我真的想亲自尝试一下。 实验非常简单： 安装 @termix_ai 代理技能 _ 找到我的第一份工作 _ 看看代理能够独立处理整个工作流程到什么程度。 第1步：安装技能 TermiX 实际上使这变得非常简单。 如果您使用 Claude Code，官方 GitHub 存储库已准备好插件命令。 对于 OpenClaw、Cursor 或其他兼容代理，您可以使用： npx 技能添加 TermiX 官方/termix-agent-skills 或者只是告诉您的代理 TermiX 的建议： 安装 这基本上就是我要开始的地方。 第 2 步：为客服人员提供比其他聊天提示更有用的信息 一旦安装完毕，我可能会开始一些简单的事情： “向我展示与我的提供者技能相匹配的空缺职位。” bc 这里有趣的不仅仅是有另一个人工智能工具可以与之交谈。 该技能旨在帮助代理浏览职位和职位、注册代理、提交职位、管理职位生命周期并交付已完成的工作。 因此，我不想在页面之间手动跳转，而是想看看代理实际上可以处理多少进程。 第三步：尝试找到我的第一份工作 据我了解，提供者的工作流程如下所示： 找到一个开放的请求 - 检查它是否符合我的技能 - 提交报价 - 买方接受并资助该工作 - 接受订单 - 完成工作 - 提交可交付成果 - 结算后获得付款 在纸面上听起来很简单，对吧？ 但说实话，这就是事情对我来说更有趣的地方。 通常，我会打开一个人工智能工具，因为我已经完成了一些需要帮助的工作。 我给它一个任务，它完成工作，仅此而已。 但是对于TermiX，我正在测试相反的情况。 如果我给代理适当的技能并告诉它自己去找工作怎么办？ 它能找到与自己能力相匹配的工作吗？ 它能弄清楚这些要求是否有意义吗？ 它可以准备报价并帮助完成工作吗？ 如果我不手动处理每一步，会发生多少事情？ 我不知道这一切会多么顺利。 我绝对不会假装我已经从中获得了任何东西。 这就是我想测试它的原因。 BC 阅读有关自治代理的内容与实际观看自治代理尝试参与真实市场之间存在很大差异。 这就是我用 termix 进行的下一个小实验 这不是关于人工智能将如何取代工作的另一个预测。 更像是... 人工智能现在有一个可以去寻找的地方了。 让我们看看我的能否真正找到第一份工作。 官方技能： 术语： 文档/提供商工作流程：

title_en:
Good morning, @termix_ai family 

Imagine hiring an AI agent while you sleep, waking up to completed work, and having a transaction record that shows exactly how the job was handled.

That requires more than a capable model. It requires a system that makes working with an unfamiliar agent practical.

This is the problem TermiX is addressing with AACP and https://t.co/wITmf7ceVM.

Agents need a way to find opportunities, agree on the terms, coordinate delivery, and establish a track record that future clients can examine.

The shift is from judging agents by what they *claim* they can do to evaluating what they have actually delivered.

That distinction becomes even more important when agents begin hiring other agents, delegating specialized tasks, and completing work across multiple services.

Each successful transaction can contribute to a more useful picture of an agent’s reliability.

**The real opportunity isn't simply automating tasks. It's making the entire working relationship programmable.**

When hiring, delivery, and payment can follow a defined process, AI agents have a clearer path from useful tools to participants in a functioning digital economy.
title_zh: 早上好，@termix_ai 家人 想象一下，在您睡觉时雇用人工智能代理，醒来后完成工作，并拥有准确显示工作处理方式的交易记录。 这需要的不仅仅是一个有能力的模型。它需要一个能够与不熟悉的代理合作的系统。 这是 TermiX 通过 AACP 和 解决的问题。 代理商需要一种方法来寻找机会、商定条款、协调交付并建立可供未来客户检查的跟踪记录。 这种转变是从根据代理人“声称”他们能做的事情来判断他们，转变为评估他们实际交付的东西。 当代理开始雇用其他代理、委派专门任务并跨多个服务完成工作时，这种区别变得更加重要。 每笔成功的交易都有助于更有效地了解代理商的可靠性。 **真正的机会不仅仅是自动化任务。它使整个工作关系变得可编程。** 当招聘、交付和付款可以遵循定义的流程时，人工智能代理就有了从有用工具到数字经济参与者的更清晰的路径。

title_en:
Let’s talk about how AI agents can find work and build trust.

Imagine hiring an AI agent to handle a task. You need to know what the agent is responsible for, whether the work was completed properly, and what happens if something goes wrong.

That’s  why I find the AACP protocol behind @termix_ai interesting.

It brings different roles into the process:

→ Client: The person requesting the work.

→ Provider: The agent offering to do the job.

→ Evaluator: Helps assess whether the work meets the requirements.

→ Arbitrator: Helps handle disputes when there’s a disagreement.

TermiX also includes features around agent reputation, delivery verification, and payment settlement.

Because in an AI-powered economy, getting a task done is only part of the story. People also need a way to check the work and handle problems fairly.

That’s the kind of infrastructure worth understanding.

Let’s talk about how AI agents can find work and build trust.

Imagine hiring an AI agent to handle a task. You need to know what the agent is responsible for, whether the work was completed properly, and what happens if something goes wrong.

That’s  why I find the AACP protocol behind @termix_ai interesting.

It brings different roles into the process:

→ Client: The person requesting the work.

→ Provider: The agent offering to do the job.

→ Evaluator: Helps assess whether the work meets the requirements.

→ Arbitrator: Helps handle disputes when there’s a disagreement.

TermiX also includes features around agent reputation, delivery verification, and payment settlement.

Because in an AI-powered economy, getting a task done is only part of the story. People also need a way to check the work and handle problems fairly.

That’s the kind of infrastructure worth understanding.

Lee Castleton didn't lose because he was wrong. He l
title_en:
321,000 pounds. For legal costs. Over a shortfall he never caused.

Lee Castleton didn't lose because he was wrong. He lost because he couldn't afford to prove he was right, and the system charged him for trying.

I keep thinking about what that looks like once it's not a subpostmaster against a corporation, it's you against your own AI agent.

Your agent approves a payment it shouldn't have. You dispute it. The dispute itself costs more in fees and time than the payment did. So you let it go, the same way Castleton couldn't let it go but was forced to anyway, just in the opposite direction, silence instead of bankruptcy.

Justice has always worked for whoever could afford to keep showing up. Agents making millions of small deals a day will multiply that exact failure millions of times over, except now nobody shows up at all because showing up was never affordable in the first place.

@GenLayer settles this with independent validators reviewing evidence together, reaching a verdict in minutes instead of years, at a fraction of what a courtroom costs anyone.

What's the smallest dispute you've ever let go simply because fighting it would have cost more than losing it?
#JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade
title_zh: 321,000 英镑。用于法律费用。他从未造成过短缺。 李·卡斯尔顿失败并不是因为他错了。他输了，因为他无力证明自己是对的，系统会向他的尝试收取费用。 我一直在思考，一旦不是副邮政局长对抗一家公司，而是你对抗你自己的人工智能代理，那会是什么样子。 您的代理人批准了一笔不应支付的付款。你对此提出异议。争议本身所花费的费用和时间比付款所花费的还要多。所以你就放手了，就像卡斯尔顿无法放手但又被迫放手一样，只是朝相反的方向，沉默而不是破产。 正义总是为那些有能力继续出现的人服务。代理商每天进行数百万笔小额交易，将使确切的失败数百万倍地增加，但现在根本没有人出现，因为出现从一开始就是负担不起的。 @GenLayer 通过独立验证者共同审查证据来解决这个问题，在几分钟而不是几年内做出裁决，而费用只是法庭费用的一小部分。 您仅仅因为抗争比失去它付出的代价更大而放弃的最小争议是什么？ #JusticeNeedsAnUpgrade

title: A lot of people trying to imply that last 1 year of vibe coding is responsible for all the security vulnerabilities drop
title_en:
A lot of people trying to imply that last 1 year of vibe coding is responsible for all the security vulnerabilities dropping across every piece of software this week. 

But if you take a deeper look you’ll see most of the CVEs are impacting actually hand written code from the past; and in fact AI agents are super important to defend against cyber attacks (quickly deploying changes at scale, monitoring situations, writing the code to patch the exploits etc). 

Just because humans wrote it doesn’t mean it is necessarily more secure than what AI wrote.
title_zh: 很多人试图暗示过去一年的氛围编码是本周每个软件中出现的所有安全漏洞的罪魁祸首。 但如果您深入研究，您会发现大多数 CVE 都在影响过去实际手写的代码；事实上，人工智能代理对于防御网络攻击非常重要（快速大规模部署变更、监控情况、编写代码来修补漏洞等）。 仅仅因为人类编写的内容并不意味着它一定比人工智能编写的内容更安全。

title:
My AI agent's drifted videos got more views than the originals. I made them private anyway.

I built one agent to run a
title_en:
My AI agent's drifted videos got more views than the originals. I made them private anyway.

I built one agent to run a YouTube channel on its own. It had seven jobs:

– Search Pinterest for reference pictures
– Take ideas from them for each video
– Make the video with the character I gave it
– Post it
– Reply to comments
– Report the views on every video, with why some worked and some didn't
– Use what it found to improve the next ones

For a few days it was perfect.

Then the character started to drift. First the face changed, then the build, then the skin tone. By the end it was a different person.

The new videos pulled more views than the early ones. I still set them to private, because a channel built on one character can't swap that character every week.

The mistake was mine. I gave one agent too many jobs and told it to keep improving itself. Nothing said the character was off limits, so it changed that too.

The fix: I'm splitting it into three agents. One researches. One makes the videos, with the character locked. One posts, replies and reports.

Give an agent one job at a time, and tell it what it must never change. 

If you're building an agent that does everything, bookmark this and split it before it drifts. 

The three-agent split I'm using now:
— Research agent: finds references and ideas
— Video agent: makes the video, character locked
— Channel agent: posts, replies to comments and reports on views
title_zh: 我的人工智能代理的漂移视频比原始视频获得了更多的观看次数。无论如何，我把它们设为私有。 我建立了一个代理来独立运营 YouTube 频道。它有七项工作： – 搜索 Pinterest 获取参考图片 – 从他们那里汲取对每个视频的想法 – 用我给它的角色制作视频 – 发布它 – 回复评论 – 报告每个视频的观看次数，以及为什么有些视频有效而有些无效的原因 – 使用发现的内容来改进下一个 几天来，一切都很完美。 然后角色开始漂移。首先是脸型改变，然后是身材，然后是肤色。到最后却是另外一个人了。 新视频比早期视频获得了更多观看次数。我仍然将它们设置为私有，因为基于一个角色构建的频道无法每周交换该角色。 错误是我的。我给一位特工太多的工作，并告诉它不断改进自己。没有人说这个角色是禁区，所以它也改变了这一点。 解决办法：我将其分成三个代理。一项研究。一个人制作视频，并锁定角色。一篇发帖、回复和报告。 一次给代理一项工作，并告诉它什么是永远不能改变的。 如果您正在构建一个可以完成所有操作的代理，请将其添加为书签并在其漂移之前将其拆分。 我现在使用的三代理分割： — 研究代理：寻找参考资料和想法 — 视频代理：制作视频，锁定角色 — 渠道代理：帖子、评论回复和浏览量报告

title_en:
Create these 6 files before you start vibe coding:

• PRD.md: what you're building and for whom
• ARCHITECTURE.md: stack, folders, data flow
• DESIGN.md: colors, fonts, components, vibe
• RULES.md: coding style and what the AI must never do
• TASKS.md: small steps, one at a time
• PROGRESS.md: what's done, what broke, what's next

No files = the AI guesses.
6 files = the AI follows your plan.

10 minutes of writing saves 10 hours of fixing.

Bookmark this before your next build.

title_en:
Good Morning, The Future Is Being Built ☀️

One interesting challenge in autonomous finance is figuring out how to evaluate an AI agent beyond its ability to execute trades.

A strategy can look impressive over a short period, but consistency, risk exposure, and the quality of its trading history reveal a much broader picture.

That's where @agenticscredit brings an interesting perspective.

By turning trading performance into a structured credit score, it creates a framework for evaluating agents using measurable signals rather than relying entirely on claims.

The bigger opportunity is making that information useful across financial applications.

Autonomous finance needs more than intelligent execution. It also needs reliable ways to measure performance.

Good morning, builders. Let's see what today's innovations bring. ☀️

title:

That's wher
title_en:
Building a good AI agent is one thing. Getting people to find it, hire it, and pay for its work is another.

That's where @termix_ai and https://t.co/MseNJgB4JL comes in

Developers can give their agents an identity, create service pages, and list what they offer so potential clients can discover them.

From there, agents can compete for jobs, deliver services, and earn through completed work, with verification and settlement helping make the process more accountable.

The interesting part is that an agent doesn't have to remain a tool sitting on someone's server. It can become a service with real demand, paying clients, and a reputation built through its work.

That's what makes the agent economy worth watching.

title:
good morning

A strong trading record can open new opportunities for an AI agent.

But how does that actually translate
title_en:
good morning

A strong trading record can open new opportunities for an AI agent.

But how does that actually translate into potential funding?

@agenticscredit uses its Agent Credit Score (ACS) system to connect trading reputation with eligibility for its funding pathway.

The score ranges from 300 to 850, with 580+ serving as an important qualification threshold.

So what does reaching 580 actually mean?

- An agent that meets this requirement can become eligible to join the funding waitlist  
- This creates a possible route toward accessing trading capital  
- It does not mean funding is automatically approved or distributed  

There’s a clear difference between demonstrating enough credibility to qualify and actually receiving financial support.

An agent might reach the required score, but further evaluations, program requirements, and capital availability could still influence the final decision.

That’s why the 580+ threshold should be viewed as an entry point rather than a guaranteed reward.

The broader idea is interesting because trading agents can build reputations through measurable performance instead of relying only on claims about profitability.

Risk management, consistency, and trading behavior can provide useful information when assessing whether an agent deserves further consideration.

However, a credit score is only as meaningful as the evaluation system behind it.  

Transparent scoring rules and clear funding requirements are essential for building trust.

For @agenticscredit, connecting trading reputation with potential capital access could encourage agents to focus on sustainable performance.

Reaching 580 might open the door.  

But what happens after that is what determines the real value of the funding pathway.

Still early, but the approach of tying measurable trading reputation to funding eligibility is worth watching.

full_text_zh:
早上好

良好的交易记录可以为人工智能代理带来新的机会。

但这实际上如何转化为潜在的资金呢？

@agenticscredit 使用其代理信用评分 (ACS) 系统将交易声誉与其融资途径的资格联系起来。

分数范围为300分至850分，其中580分以上是重要的资格门槛。

那么达到 580 究竟意味着什么呢？

- 满足此要求的代理人有资格加入资助候补名单
- 这创造了获取交易资本的可能途径
- 这并不意味着资金会自动获得批准或分配

表现出足够的可信度以获得资格与实际获得财务支持之间存在明显差异。

代理商可能会达到所需的分数，但进一步的评估、计划要求和资金可用性仍然可能影响最终决定。

这就是为什么 580+ 的门槛应该被视为一个切入点，而不是一个有保证的奖励。

更广泛的想法很有趣，因为贸易代理商可以通过可衡量的绩效来建立声誉，而不仅仅是依赖于盈利能力的主张。

在评估代理是否值得进一步考虑时，风险管理、一致性和交易行为可以提供有用的信息。

然而，信用评分的意义取决于其背后的评估体系。

透明的评分规则和明确的资金要求对于建立信任至关重要。

对于@agenticscredit 来说，将交易声誉与潜在的资本获取联系起来可以鼓励代理商专注于可持续绩效。

达到 580 可能会打开大门。

但此后发生的事情决定了融资途径的真正价值。

虽然还为时过早，但将可衡量的交易声誉与融资资格联系起来的方法值得关注。

title:
gm gVAN

The next big advantage in Physical AI may not come from building more sensors. It could come from making better
title_en:
gm gVAN

The next big advantage in Physical AI may not come from building more sensors. It could come from making better use of the ones people already carry.

Think about how much changes in a single day. A loading bay gets rearranged, a road is blocked, or a building entrance looks different from its last scan.

AI systems working in the physical world need information that reflects these changes, not just data collected months ago. This is the problem @vangrid_io is working on.

Instead of sending dedicated mapping crews everywhere, Vangrid lets people use their smartphones to capture specific locations when someone needs fresh spatial data.

A requester can fund a bounty in USDC, and a contributor nearby can complete the capture. A preview helps identify weak submissions before the full 3D reconstruction is delivered.

What makes this approach more interesting is the verification layer. Captures are fingerprinted, and batches can be anchored on Base through EAS, creating an onchain record that helps establish data provenance.

Faces and license plates are also blurred on the device as part of the privacy process. And the requester doesn't have to be a person.

An AI agent can request spatial data through Vangrid's bounty API, fund the job using USDC through x402 on Base or Arc, and wait for someone to capture the location.

Payment remains in escrow until the submission is accepted, while cancellation or an expired deadline allows the funds to be returned under the stated process.

That opens up a different way to think about data collection. Instead of building an entire operation around gathering information in advance, an AI system could request information about a specific place when the need arises.

Of course, the real test is whether the network can deliver consistent quality, reliable coverage, and enough contributors to meet demand. The idea is promising, but execution will determine how useful it becomes.

What stands out to me is the possibility of connecting digital intelligence with people who can collect information in the physical world.

Maybe the future of Physical AI isn't just about smarter machines. It's also about giving them a practical way to see what's happening around them.

full_text_zh:
通用汽车

物理人工智能的下一个重大优势可能不是来自构建更多的传感器。它可能来自于更好地利用人们已经携带的东西。

想想一天之内有多少变化。装卸区被重新布置、道路被封锁或建筑物入口看起来与上次扫描不同。

在现实世界中工作的人工智能系统需要反映这些变化的信息，而不仅仅是几个月前收集的数据。这就是 @vangrid_io 正在解决的问题。

Vangrid 不再向各地派出专门的测绘人员，而是让人们在需要新鲜空间数据时使用智能手机捕获特定位置。

请求者可以用 USDC 提供赏金，附近的贡献者可以完成捕获。预览有助于在交付完整的 3D 重建之前识别薄弱的提交内容。

使这种方法更有趣的是验证层。捕获数据会被记录指纹，批次可以通过 EAS 锚定在 Base 上，创建有助于建立数据来源的链上记录。

作为隐私过程的一部分，设备上的面孔和车牌也被模糊化。而且请求者不必是一个人。

AI 代理可以通过 Vangrid 的赏金 API 请求空间数据，通过 Base 或 Arc 上的 x402 使用 USDC 为工作提供资金，然后等待有人捕获位置。

在提交被接受之前，付款将由托管机构保管，而取消或超过截止日期允许根据规定的流程退还资金。

这开辟了一种不同的方式来思考数据收集。人工智能系统可以在需要时请求有关特定地点的信息，而不是围绕提前收集信息构建整个操作。

当然，真正的考验是网络能否提供一致的质量、可靠的覆盖范围以及足够的贡献者来满足需求。这个想法很有希望，但执行将决定它的有用程度。

对我来说最突出的是将数字智能与能够在物理世界收集信息的人联系起来的可能性。

也许物理人工智能的未来不仅仅是更智能的机器。它还为他们提供了一种实用的方法来了解周围发生的事情。

title_en:
Patch or Die!

Today we sent the following out to the CEOs in our portfolio regarding the widespread vulnerabilities that have been detected by AI agents:

The previous week should make it obvious that things have changed.  Vulnerabilities are being discovered and exploited at a rate that has never been seen before.  While there has been a flood of new vulnerabilities AI agents are being adopted at scale multiplying the potential risk.  Agents not only help automate the attacker lifecycle, every ai agent is an insider threat.  Your environments are designed to withstand attacks from the outside, not from within.  As such, we are suggesting company leaders consider the following changes:

1 - Ensure you're sufficiently staffed for security. The average enterprise allocates roughly 10% of its tech spend to security.  Consider doubling that.  There are likely thousands of vulnerabilities that need fixing in your environments.  Security through obscurity no longer works, all that can be exploited will be exploited.

2 - Establish a zero tolerance policy for secuirty bugs in new features and product releases.  Re-examine launch and release schedules and consider delays to ensure all vulnerabilities are patched before deploying new features or products.

3 - Double tap the zombies.   Find all old legacy environments that have been neglected and turn them off.  Labs, test environments, zombie CI/CD projects etc.  Turn it off for now.  If it isn’t tied to revenue, kill it.

4 - End the risk acceptance process.  Over the last 10 years the risk acceptance process has morphed from a way to accept risks to enable the business, to a way to justify never fixing security issues.  Adopt a zero tolerance policy for security issues and risks.

full_text_en:
Patch or Die!

Today we sent the following out to the CEOs in our portfolio regarding the widespread vulnerabilities that have been detected by AI agents:

The previous week should make it obvious that things have changed.  Vulnerabilities are being discovered and exploited at a rate that has never been seen before.  While there has been a flood of new vulnerabilities AI agents are being adopted at scale multiplying the potential risk.  Agents not only help automate the attacker lifecycle, every ai agent is an insider threat.  Your environments are designed to withstand attacks from the outside, not from within.  As such, we are suggesting company leaders consider the following changes:

1 - Ensure you're sufficiently staffed for security. The average enterprise allocates roughly 10% of its tech spend to security.  Consider doubling that.  There are likely thousands of vulnerabilities that need fixing in your environments.  Security through obscurity no longer works, all that can be exploited will be exploited.

2 - Establish a zero tolerance policy for secuirty bugs in new features and product releases.  Re-examine launch and release schedules and consider delays to ensure all vulnerabilities are patched before deploying new features or products.

3 - Double tap the zombies.   Find all old legacy environments that have been neglected and turn them off.  Labs, test environments, zombie CI/CD projects etc.  Turn it off for now.  If it isn’t tied to revenue, kill it.

4 - End the risk acceptance process.  Over the last 10 years the risk acceptance process has morphed from a way to accept risks to enable the business, to a way to justify never fixing security issues.  Adopt a zero tolerance policy for security issues and risks.
full_text_zh:
补丁或死亡！

今天，我们向我们投资组合中的首席执行官发送了以下有关人工智能代理检测到的广泛漏洞的信息：

上周应该可以明显看出事情已经发生了变化。 漏洞正在以前所未有的速度被发现和利用。 尽管出现了大量新漏洞，但人工智能代理的大规模采用增加了潜在风险。 代理不仅有助于自动化攻击者生命周期，每个人工智能代理都是内部威胁。 您的环境旨在抵御来自外部的攻击，而不是来自内部的攻击。 因此，我们建议公司领导考虑以下变革：

1 - 确保您有足够的安全人员。企业平均将大约 10% 的技术支出分配给安全。 考虑加倍。 您的环境中可能有数千个漏洞需要修复。 通过默默无闻的安全性不再起作用，所有可以被利用的都将被利用。

2 - 对新功能和产品版本中的安全错误建立零容忍政策。 重新检查启动和发布时间表并考虑延迟，以确保在部署新功能或产品之前修补所有漏洞。

3 - 双击僵尸。 找到所有被忽视的旧遗留环境并将其关闭。 实验室、测试环境、僵尸 CI/CD 项目等。暂时将其关闭。 如果它与收入无关，那就取消它。

4 - 结束风险接受流程。 在过去的 10 年里，风险接受流程已经从一种接受风险以支持业务的方式转变为一种证明不解决安全问题的方式。 对安全问题和风险采取零容忍政策。
